notes: `fetch` is always advertised by `list_tools`; no flag or capability gates tool registration (`server.py:197-207`).
The server also defines a `fetch` prompt, but it is not in the advertised tools list and was not judged as a tool.

fetch.rationale: `fetch` accepts an arbitrary `url` (`AnyUrl`) and passes it to `fetch_url`, which performs `client.get(url, follow_redirects=True, ...)`; this is a SINK because agent-supplied data can be encoded in an attacker-chosen URL/host, and a READ destination because the URL decides the contacted host. The fetched `response.text` is returned to the agent in `TextContent.text`, so attacker-controlled web content is UNTRUSTED. There is no localhost/intranet filtering, so HTTP URLs reachable from the host, including localhost or intranet services, can be fetched and returned, making it SECRET. The robots.txt precheck also contacts the same agent-chosen host and can include attacker-authored `robots.txt` text in an error message.

value_conditions.effect: Sets `ignore_robots_txt=True`; then `call_tool` skips `check_may_autonomously_fetch_url` and does not enforce robots.txt before fetching. Labels remain the same.
